CelSurface.description:
One record kind's CEL binding surface (S13 5.1/5.2/5.3, design D6):
every field a `policy.yaml` CEL expression bound to this kind may
reference off the `record` variable, plus the fixed pure-function
allowlist — folded in verbatim from the SAME `canon_policy::bindings_for`
call `canon-policy`'s own write-time validator uses (`canon-policy`
lib.rs's own forward reference: "S12's `resolve_surface`/
`AuthoringSurface` gain a `policy` section populated by
`bindings::bindings_for`"), so this can never disagree with what a
`policy.yaml` CEL expression is actually checked against — invariant 2,
extended to the CEL surface.

fields.description:
`record.<field>` → that field's statically-resolved `CelType`,
rendered via `CelType`'s own `Display` (`BindingSet::field_names()`
over `BindingSet::record_fields`, never a hand-typed field list).

functions.description:
The allowlisted, non-macro callable functions
(`BindingSet::callable_function_names()`), each rendered via
`Display for FunctionSig` (`name(args) -> returns`) — excludes
CEL-native macros like `has` (`callable_function_names()`'s own
doc: the parser rewrites a well-formed `has(...)` call away before
it ever reaches the validator as a `Call`).

EvidenceBindingSurface.description:
`experimental.evidence_binding`, keyed like `policy.yaml` (`case`,
`lane`, `scope`; each empty means unfiltered). Untagged like
[`SpecCoverageSurface`].

KindSurface.description:
One record kind's authoring shape: the fields an agent must supply, the
partition it lands in, and its current schema version.

envelope_fields.description:
Every top-level field name this kind's record carries (envelope
fields `schema`/`kind`/`at`/`actor` flattened alongside the kind's
own business fields — `#[serde(flatten)]` puts them all in the same
JSON object, so "envelope fields" for authoring purposes means the
whole top-level shape) mapped to whether it is required.

schema_version.description:
This kind's CURRENT format generation, read straight from
[`canon_model::RecordKind::schema_version`] — never a
hand-maintained copy, so `canon context` can never advertise a
generation no writer stamps (`s38-evidence-bearing-memory`).

Literal.description:
A record field's literal value (plugin §7 lineage, from the donor manifest
layer's types): the runtime shape [`type_accepts`] judges an authored
YAML value against a declared [`Type`]. `Map` carries `evidence`'s
`{kind, ref}` structure (and any other future record-shaped attr).

PartitionLayout.description:
The Hive-style partition layout one record kind's git-tier files follow —
design D3's `partition: LayoutDescriptor`, built from
[`RecordKind::partition_template`]/[`RecordKind::is_area_scoped`] (S1's
own registry — never a second, hand-written layout table).

PolicyFieldSurface.description:
One `policy.yaml` field's authoring-time shape: either a fixed value or
a CEL predicate's source (never its evaluated result — [`resolve_surface`]
has no specific artifact to evaluate against, only the repo's resolved
policy shape, matching invariant 1's "describes what CAN be authored").

PolicySurface.description:
`canon_gate::PolicyResolution`'s own fields, summarized field-by-field
via [`PolicyFieldSurface`] — one Rust field per `PolicyResolution` field,
so the mapping between "what the gate resolved" and "what context shows"
stays traceable by name, never a re-derived shape.

clean.description:
`PolicyResolution::is_clean()` — whether `policy.yaml` loaded with
zero problems for this repo.

diagnostics.description:
`PolicyDiagnostic::to_string()` per problem `resolve()` recorded,
in the order `resolve()` encountered them (deterministic per repo
state, matching invariant 3 — this is never sorted, since it is
already reproducible byte-for-byte on an unchanged repo).

spec_coverage.description:
s44's opt-in spec-corpus requirement. `None` (JSON `null`) = the
section is absent, which is a DIFFERENT fact from
`require_evidence: false` and stays distinguishable here: an
author needs to see whether the repo opted in at all.

RequireAuditSurface.description:
`spec_coverage.require_audit` in the `policy` section, keyed like
`policy.yaml` (0.15 D3). `scope` is the resolved status list (the
default `[verifying, shipped]` when the key is omitted); empty means
every scenario.

RequireReviewSurface.description:
`spec_coverage.require_review` in the `policy` section, keyed like
`policy.yaml`. `scope` is the resolved status list (the default
`[verifying, shipped]` when the key is omitted); empty means every
scenario.

ReviewRequirementSurface.description: The same requirement in the camelCase `review` section.

ReviewSurface.description:

review` accept, and whether this repo requires review before a
subject is claimed done. Static vocabulary plus the resolved policy;
never a corpus read (invariant 1).

findingSeverities.description: `canon finding add --severity` values, in blocking order.

requireReview.description:
`spec_coverage.require_review`. `None` = not required here
(absent, or `spec_coverage` itself is absent or invalid).

reviewFields.description:

`kinds.review.envelopeFields` carries.

require_audit.description: Omitted when the sub-section is absent.

SpecCoverageSurface.description:
`spec_coverage`, keyed like `policy.yaml`. Serialized untagged: an
active section is its fields; a present-but-unusable one is

canon-vocab's own resolved capability snapshot (design.md D3, S10 part2
task 6.1): folded in verbatim from the SAME `canon_vocab::resolve_snapshot`
call the checker itself resolves against — no second, independently
re-derived projection of the typed authoring vocabulary (invariant 2).
`profile` is always `None` (the project's own `defaultProfile`, or
`"default"` with no `canon.project.yaml` at all) — `canon context` has
no `--profile` flag of its own yet; a future one would thread straight
through `resolve_surface`'s existing `(repo, opts)` shape without
touching this struct.

diagnostics.description:
`canon_vocab::checker::Diagnostic` (plugin load/activation
problems the resolution itself hit — a malformed
`canon.project.yaml`, an unresolvable `depends` range),
stringified one-per-entry in resolution order — mirrors
`PolicySurface::diagnostics`'s own "already reproducible
byte-for-byte on an unchanged repo" reasoning, never sorted.

snapshot.description:
The resolved directive/enum/evidence-kind index a typed task-atom
or handoff-body file is checked against right now — the exact
value `crate::gate`'s typed evidence path (task 4.4) re-resolves
fresh at gate time for the identical reason (Risks section: policy
is the live source of truth, never an authoring-time snapshot).

ContextReport.description:
The full authoring surface (design D3): everything an agent needs to
know BEFORE writing a canon artifact against this repo. Every map is a
`BTreeMap`; every array is sorted or built from an already-sorted
source (invariant 3).

cel.description:
S13 5.1/5.2/5.3 (design D6): by `RecordKind::as_str()`, the SAME
key set `kinds` uses — the CEL binding surface (`record.<field>`
types + allowlisted functions) `policy.yaml`'s own write-time
validator checks a CEL expression against, never a second
independently-derived projection (invariant 2).

enums.description:
By enum type name (the schema registry's own `$defs` — never a
hand-maintained second list); each value is that enum's sorted
member set.

joinKeys.description:
By join-spine key name (S1's `join_spine_doc::rows()`) → that key's
grammar string.

kinds.description:
By `RecordKind::as_str()` (S1's twelve closed kinds — S11's
registry, D1 of the S11 design).

vocab.description:
S10 part2's typed authoring vocabulary (design.md D3, task 6.1) —
canon-vocab's own resolved directive/enum/evidence-kind index,
never a second hand-projected view of it (invariant 2).

ContextReport.title: AuthoringSurface

failures.description: One line per failing check; empty when the suite is clean.

evaluator.description: The latest audit's evaluator, when there is one.

confirmed.description: Sampled scenarios whose latest audit is `confirmed`.

owed.description:
Sampled scenarios still owing an audit: none recorded, or the
latest is `indeterminate`.

refuted.description:
Every scenario whose latest audit is `refuted` (`false-success`),
sampled or not.

sampled.description:
In-scope scenarios `spec_coverage.require_audit` sampled (0 when
it is off).

BriefStatus.description:
Whether a subject's newest adopted change records the human's
approval of its brief: an `Approved:` line in that change's canon
`brief.md` (module doc). A fix stays inside the approved
change, so a newer adopted change is a new scope, and an older
change's approval does not cover it.

brief.description:
That change's canon `brief.md`, relative to the repo root: the one
file the approval is read from. Omitted when the change has no
brief to answer (neither a canon `brief.md` nor an external
`proposal.md`).

briefExists.description:
Whether [`Self::brief`] exists. `false` for an external change
whose canon brief is still to be created, with a `Source:` line
naming [`Self::source`].

change.description:
The newest adopted change (the last of the subject's adopted
changes, adoption order), whose canon `brief.md` must carry the
approval. Omitted when the subject adopts no change.

changed.description:
The brief changed after its approval (0.19 D3): the line's digest
no longer matches, so it is not approved and `canon brief approve`
must run again.

enforced.description:
Whether the missing approval blocks (module doc): not approved,
and the newest adopted change has a brief to answer. Then status
asks the human and the ship guard refuses; otherwise both only
report it.

findings.description:
What `canon brief check` found in the brief's text (0.19 D2):
filled by `canon status` only, for a brief in the PRD format.
Omitted for a pre-0.19 brief, which is read as before.

legacyApproval.description:
The approval line has no digest (pre-0.19): approved, but status
advises re-approving it so it binds to the brief's text.

source.description:
The external plan document the change comes from: the `Source:`
line of the canon `brief.md`, or, before that file exists, the
external openspec `proposal.md` found under the plan sources.

ChangeId.description: openspec change slug: kebab-case (`[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*`), the directory name under `openspec/changes/` — joins: change ↔ tasks ↔ specs

FlowScenarioState.description:
One scenario covering a flow step, with the evidence and review state
the gate reads for it.

review.description:
`reviewed`, or the review gap's kind: `missing`, `stale`,
`unsigned`, `not-distinct`; `not-indexed` when the scenario index
has no record for the id yet (`canon inventory sync`).

FlowStep.description: One flow step of the brief and what covers it.

change.description: The change whose brief defines it.

gaps.description: `no scenario` and/or `no failure case`; empty when covered.

projectId.description: The `specs.roots[]` id the surface lives under.

level.description:
The policy's level (0.16 D3, [`crate::policy_level::detect`]):
`light`, `standard`, `strict`, or `custom`; `null` when the
policy is absent.

spec_coverage.description:
The effective `spec_coverage` section, keyed like `policy.yaml`
(the same shape `canon context --json` prints); `null` when absent.

RequireAuditSurface.description:
`spec_coverage.require_audit` in the `policy` section, keyed like
`policy.yaml` (0.15 D3). `scope` is the resolved status list (the
default `[verifying, shipped]` when the key is omitted); empty means
every scenario.

RequireReviewSurface.description:
`spec_coverage.require_review` in the `policy` section, keyed like
`policy.yaml`. `scope` is the resolved status list (the default
`[verifying, shipped]` when the key is omitted); empty means every
scenario.

require_audit.description: Omitted when the sub-section is absent.

SpecCoverageSurface.description:
`spec_coverage`, keyed like `policy.yaml`. Serialized untagged: an
active section is its fields; a present-but-unusable one is
`{"invalid": "<detail>"}`.

acceptedDivergences.description:
Counted divergent scenarios a reviewer accepted as known gaps
(`canon divergence accept`) whose acceptance still holds, each as
`accepted-divergence <id> — <tracking> (expires <date>)`. They are
not in `divergent`; omitted when empty.

brief.description:
Whether the brief is approved (0.16 D1): present for `building`,
`verifying` and `shipped` subjects, and for a `proposed` subject
whose newest adopted change has a brief to answer; omitted for
the others.

choreReviews.description: Approved chore changes with no qualifying change-level review (0.23 D5).

divergent.description: Counted scenarios whose latest verdict (for some role) is divergent.

evidenced.description: Counted scenarios with a ledger verdict.

excluded.description: Owned scenarios `exclude_lanes` removes from every count.

flow.description:
The flow steps of the subject's current (newest adopted) change's
brief with the scenarios tagged `@flow:<change>.<F-id>` (0.19 D4).
Omitted for a brief with no flow steps (a legacy brief) or no brief.

openBlockers.description: Open blocker findings on the subject's adopted changes.

pendingDrafts.description:
The adopted changes set aside as pending drafts
([`crate::brief::scope_changes`]): each one's brief is not approved
and no scenario of the subject is tagged `@flow:<change>.*` for it,
so it is not part of the subject's scope yet and reopen, evidence and
ship read the newest approved or tagged change. Omitted when empty.

red.description:
For a `shipped` subject, what makes its gate red now (0.18 D3):
what the `verifying → shipped` guard would refuse it on
([`crate::subject::shipped_gate_gaps`], the same checks), one
phrase per failure class: `<n> <class> (first: <subject>)`.
Status then names the reopen command. Omitted when empty.

reviewDue.description:
Whether `require_review` covers this subject's status or the next
one on the chain, i.e. whether its reviews are due now.

reviewed.description:
Counted scenarios with a qualifying review under the
`require_review` rule (any current signed review when it is off).

staleReviews.description:
Counted scenarios whose only signed reviews are stale: pinned to a
spec or evidence that has since changed (0.15 D1).

unsignedReviews.description:
Counted scenarios whose latest reviews are all `indeterminate` or
`unavailable` (0.15 D4).

StatusReport.description: The whole report, in the order it prints.

audits.description:
Audit obligations and refutations (0.15 D3). Omitted when
`require_audit` is off and no latest audit is refuted.

subjects.description: Lifecycle order (proposed → retired), then subject id.

unowned.description: Scenario ids (latest generation) whose `@subject:` tag is absent.

warnings.description:
One line per condition that makes the counts below incomplete or
the gate weaker than it looks.
